name: US-Twt
site_description: The Twitchell Island site is a rice paddy that is owned by the state and managed by the California Department of Water Resources. While Bare Peat field was leveled for rice planting, the tower was installed on April 3, 2009. The rice paddy was converted from corn in 2007. In Summer 2009, Bispyribac-sodium and Pendimethalin herbicides were applied to the fields prior to rice planting and flooding, then pesticide and fertilizer application took place. Each year after rice is planted in the spring by drilling, the field is flooded. Then, the field is drained in early fall, rice is harvested, and the field site is moved. Published site characterization describes Twitchell Island rice fields on Euic, thermic, Typic Haplosaprists (Rindge mucky silt loam) in a subsided Delta peatland protected by levees.
notes: Exact-site publication reports spring drill seeding, growing-season flooding, late-summer drainage for harvest, and winter reflooding for straw decomposition and wildfowl habitat.

name: US-Bi1
site_description: An agricultural field in the San Joaquin Sacramento Delta.  The field is a mix of organic peat and sediments and minerals from old river channels Exact-site publication describes a conventional perennial alfalfa field on highly degraded peatland soils, with Ryde soils as the dominant soil series.
notes: Publication-derived metadata indicates periodic flood irrigation during the growing season, repeated alfalfa cuttings with most aboveground biomass removed, and winter grazing.

name: US-Bi2
site_description:
Corn field on Bouldin Island in the Sacramento San Joaquin Delta.  This site has deep peat that was drained for farming. Over the past 100 years there has been excessive subsidence of the peat in the Delta region. The corn is usually harvested for silage cattle feed.
Corn was planted in the field 2017-2023. Sorghum was planted in the field 2024. Exact-site publication describes an organic-rich peat corn field with a short, intensive growing period and fallow-season rewetting.
notes: Publication-derived metadata indicates fallow-season flooding in autumn followed by drainage in spring, intensive potassium and nitrogen fertilization, and silage-oriented harvest context from the site page.
